name: MAS-FIRE: Fault Injection and Reliability Evaluation for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Jin Jia, Zhiling Deng, Zhuangbin Chen (corresponding), Yingqi Wang, Zibin Zheng — Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, Guangdong, China
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.SE / cs.AI); BibTeX lists it as @inproceedings, but no peer-reviewed venue confirmed as of mid-2026
reflection_type: none (this is a failure-analysis / fault-injection evaluation framework, not a reflection method). It does, however, empirically characterize the self-correction / fault-tolerant behaviors of existing MAS, including iterative critique-refine loops (Table-Critic) and reasoning-level self-detection of semantic faults.
feedback_source: n/a for the framework itself (it injects faults rather than learning from them). The MAS it evaluates use mixed feedback sources: environment error feedback / automatic retry (tool errors), critic-agent judge signals (Table-Critic), and shared-context retrieval (MetaGPT message pool). Ground truth is used only for scoring task success (HumanEval, WikiTQ, WebShop).
iteration_structure: n/a for the framework (single-pass fault injection per task, single-trial Pass@1 evaluation). The evaluated MAS span single-shot linear pipelines (MetaGPT, Camel) and iterative-refine closed loops (Table-Critic critic-refiner).
reflection_object: n/a — the paper does not modify a reflection target. What MAS-FIRE manipulates (to expose fault tolerance) is: prompts/context (system + user prompts), agent runtime outputs (reasoning chains, planning outputs, tool calls), and message routing. The fault-tolerant behaviors it observes act on action trajectory, reasoning chain, and inter-agent messages.
learning_locus: n/a (analysis/evaluation framework — no learning signal; no weight update and no in-context experience accumulation in the framework itself)
requires_training: none (no training; the framework runs and perturbs off-the-shelf MAS with GPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3 backbones; GPT-5-mini is used as a semantic-fault injector and GPT-5 as an LLM-as-a-judge annotator, neither is fine-tuned)
reward_or_critic_model: none for the framework. Evaluation uses an LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-5) to label fault-tolerant behaviors in execution logs, validated against human annotation at Cohen's Kappa = 0.94. Task success is scored against ground-truth benchmark answers.
distillation_target: none (no reusable learned artifact is distilled). The reusable outputs are conceptual: a 15-type fault taxonomy, a four-tier fault-tolerance behavioral taxonomy, and process-level robustness metrics (RS, Occurrence, Local Success, Success).
emergent_vs_engineered: n/a — neither. MAS-FIRE engineers fault injectors (scaffold-engineered perturbations via prompt modification, response rewriting, message routing) and then observes whether the target MAS's fault tolerance is architecture/rule-engineered (mechanism/rule tiers) or model-reasoning-driven (prompt/reasoning tiers). It explicitly decouples engineered structural resilience from emergent model-reasoning resilience.
memory_type: n/a for the framework. Among evaluated systems: MetaGPT uses a shared message pool (long-term, globally accessible scratchpad/context) that the paper finds buffers Memory Faults; Camel uses sequential bilateral dialogue (short-term context only); Table-Critic uses an iterative critique loop.
memory_persistence: n/a (no cross-episode memory in the framework). Evaluated MAS persist context within-episode (within a task run); MetaGPT's shared message pool keeps globally accessible context across agents within a task.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a for the framework. The paper notes MetaGPT performs rule-based message deduplication / role-based subscription filtering (retrieval-gated / rule-filtered context), and that aggressive context compression (a 'Context Length Violation' fault) is itself an injected failure mode.
error_localization_granularity: Multi-granularity by design: agent-level (multi-agent; intra-agent vs inter-agent fault split), step-level (faults injected at specific execution points — planning output, tool call, message), and response-level (response rewriting). Diagnosis is process-level via the (Occurrence, Local-Success, Success) triplet plus a four-tier (mechanism/rule/prompt/reasoning) attribution of where resilience originates.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (faults are injected and recovery is observed within a single task run; single-trial Pass@1). No cross-task experience transfer is studied. 'Intra-agent vs inter-agent' in the paper refers to fault location, not learning transfer.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: Studies mid-trajectory recovery (in-flight): the framework measures whether MAS detect injected faults and correct them during execution (e.g., automatic retry on tool errors, Table-Critic's closed-loop critique-refinement, downstream agents compensating). Local Success Rate (L_f) vs Success Rate (S_f) explicitly captures whether in-flight recovery translates to end-to-end success.
task_domains: code generation (MetaGPT), table QA / multi-step table reasoning (Table-Critic), web navigation / decision-making in simulated e-commerce (Camel); broadly software-engineering reliability of LLM multi-agent systems
benchmarks: HumanEval (164 tasks, MetaGPT code gen); WikiTableQuestions / WikiTQ (400 sampled from 4,344, Table-Critic); WebShop (251 tasks, AgentBoard-annotated version, Camel)
headline_result: Iterative, closed-loop topologies neutralize over 40% of faults that cause catastrophic collapse in linear workflows. Concretely, for Planning Faults Table-Critic's critique loop keeps RS > 89% while MetaGPT's linear pipeline drops to 43.84% (Delta RS ~ +45%); for Memory/Critical-Info-Loss faults MetaGPT's shared message pool keeps RS > 90% vs Camel's ~67% (Delta RS ~ +25%). Configuration/Instruction faults collapse linear MAS to RS as low as 0.0%.
baselines: Compared across three representative MAS architectures (MetaGPT hierarchical/linear pipeline; Table-Critic iterative critic-refiner closed loop; Camel bilateral role-play) and two foundation models (GPT-5 vs DeepSeek-V3). Fault-free baseline success rates: MetaGPT 99.0%/89.0%, Table-Critic 87.0%/78.3%, Camel 37.8%/33.0% (GPT-5/DeepSeek-V3). No prior fault-injection framework baseline; positioned against outcome-only evaluation (AgentBench, AgentBoard, AppWorld, ScienceAgentBench, OpenJudge) and prior injection work (AutoInject).
gains_vs_baseline: Architectural deltas (vs strongest comparable architecture under same fault): iterative critique loop +~45% RS over linear pipeline on Planning Faults; shared message pool +~25% RS on Critical Information Loss; +~17% average RS for stronger model (GPT-5) on semantic faults with shared-pool architectures (Hallucination +22.05%: 45.34% vs 23.29%; Inexecutable Plan +12.06%: 55.90% vs 43.84%). Counterintuitive reversal: under Blind Trust, weaker DeepSeek-V3 beats GPT-5 by 64.29% (70.61% vs 6.32%) because GPT-5's strict instruction-following obeys the corrupted directive.
compute_cost_profile: [uncertain] — the paper does not report token/API-call multipliers or training cost. It states all evaluations are single-trial (Pass@1) and that fault injection achieved a 99% success rate, with semantic faults injected by GPT-5-mini and behavior annotation done by GPT-5 (LLM-as-judge), but gives no quantitative compute/cost figures.
known_limitations: Single-trial (Pass@1) evaluation despite non-deterministic agents (no variance/repeated-run reporting); only three MAS and two backbone models; Communication Faults injectable only into MetaGPT (others lack a communication module); some tool-faults inapplicable to tasks without tool calls; ~1% injection failures re-executed; fault-tolerant behavior taxonomy derived via Grounded Theory by the authors (potential subjectivity, mitigated by kappa=0.94 LLM-judge agreement); WikiTQ sub-sampled to 400 of 4,344. Findings are correlational/diagnostic, not a remediation method.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: For the framework: ground-truth-oracle is used to score whether tasks remain successful (RS), and an LLM-judge (with human-validated labels) to attribute behaviors. The fault-tolerance the framework observes in MAS spans intrinsic self-verify (reasoning-level), external-tool/verifier (environment retry, critic agent), and rule-based filters; the key finding is that semantically-valid-but-incorrect faults bypass mechanism/rule filters and rely solely on model reasoning (Reasoning-Level FT, O_f = 100%).
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent and architecture-dependent. Mechanism/rule-tier defenses give near-certain recovery for structural faults (Communication Faults RS > 93%, tool-format L_f = 100%). Reasoning-tier self-correction is the sole defense for semantic faults but has low detection in linear pipelines. Crucially, stronger instruction-following can be net-negative: under Blind Trust, GPT-5's compliance collapses RS to 6.32% while non-compliant DeepSeek-V3 recovers to 70.61% (correction degrades with model strength when recovery requires disobeying a corrupted directive).
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not study probabilistic calibration / confidence). It does document an analogous 'reasoning tax'-style failure: superior models' strict instruction adherence makes them MORE vulnerable to prompt-level corruption (Blind Trust), an over-compliance liability rather than a calibration metric.
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (15-type fault taxonomy across 7 categories: intra-agent Planning/Memory/Reasoning/Action; inter-agent Configuration/Instruction/Communication) AND attributes-failing-step / source-of-resilience via the four-tier (mechanism/rule/prompt/reasoning) fault-tolerance attribution, plus attributes-responsible-agent through intra- vs inter-agent localization and process-level (O_f, L_f, S_f) diagnosis. It does not perform counterfactual localization of an organic failure (faults are injected, not attributed post-hoc to an unknown cause).
failure_mode_addressed: 15 injected fault types: Role Ambiguity, Blind Trust (Configuration); Instruction Logic Conflict, Instruction Ambiguity (Instruction); Inexecutable Plan, Critical Information Loss (Planning); Memory Loss, Context Length Violation (Memory); Hallucination (Reasoning); Tool Selection Error, Parameter Filling Error, Parameter Format Error (Action); Message Cycle, Message Storm, Message Broadcast Amplification (Communication). Cross-links to MAST-style modes: inter-agent misalignment (Blind Trust, Role Ambiguity), information withholding / context loss (Critical Info Loss, Memory Loss), reasoning drift / hallucination, error loops / no termination (Message Cycle), and superficial self-reflection (Judge accepts erroneous reasoning ~93.68% of failed Blind-Trust cases).
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — experimental data and fault-injection artifacts released at https://github.com/wxhhxn/MASFIRE (execution-log corpus spanning 15 fault types x 3 MAS architectures x 2 foundation models, with the fault taxonomy, behavior definitions, and metrics). Not a fixed held-out benchmark like Who&When; it is a reusable injection framework + log corpus.
builds_on: Fault injection / chaos engineering and mutation testing (Meiklejohn ServiceLevel FI, MicroFI, IntelliFT); MAS failure studies (Cemri et al. 'Why do multi-agent LLM systems fail?' / MAST; AutoInject — Huang et al. 'On the Resilience of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration with Faulty Agents', ICML 2025; TRAIL); the evaluated MAS frameworks themselves (MetaGPT, Table-Critic, CAMEL); outcome-oriented MAS evaluation (AgentBench, AgentBoard, AppWorld, ScienceAgentBench, OpenJudge); LLM self-correction limits (Huang et al. 'LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet').
extended_by_or_inspired: [uncertain] — too recent (submitted 23 Feb 2026); no indexed follow-up citations found on Semantic Scholar as of mid-2026.
citation_count: 0 (Semantic Scholar Corpus ID 285973197 shows 62 outbound references and no indexed inbound citations; very recent preprint, Feb 2026)
reasoning_model_native: Partially relevant: GPT-5 is one of the two evaluated backbones and the paper's most distinctive finding concerns strong, instruction-following ('reasoning-capable') models being MORE fragile under prompt corruption (Blind Trust). However, the framework is model-agnostic and not specifically designed for o1/R1-style built-in reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: n/a — no distillation or on-policy skill optimization; this is an evaluation/diagnostic framework, not a training method.
sample_efficiency: n/a (no learning iterations). Evaluation scale: single-trial Pass@1 over 164 (HumanEval) + 400 (WikiTQ sampled) + 251 (WebShop) tasks x 15 fault types x 3 MAS x 2 models; ~99% injection success rate.
